top_entities.name: Pakistan
top_entities.news_summary: Committee to Protect Journalists reported that Pakistani journalists Razi Tahir and Muhammad Saif, who had been reporting on unrest and an internet shutdown in Pakistan-administered Kashmir, were seized by men in police uniform and taken to an undisclosed location in Islamabad on August 1, 2026. Islamabad police have not acknowledged the detention and the journalists' whereabouts remain unknown as of CPJ's report -- part of what CPJ's Afghanistan-Pakistan representative called an escalating effort to silence independent Kashmir reporting.

top_entities.name: Wesco International
top_entities.news_summary: Ransomware group ExfilSquad claimed responsibility for a data breach at Wesco International, with the suspected attack occurring July 26, 2026 and public claims first reported July 27, 2026. The group claims exfiltration of roughly 2.6 million records (~40GB) containing customer and employee PII, account/contact data, CRM profiles, and business/credit identifiers; attorneys are investigating a potential class action. Wesco has not confirmed the full scope of the incident.

top_entities.name: GEO Group
top_entities.news_summary: Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, 41, an El Salvadoran national with a pending work-permit application and a 12-year-old daughter, died August 1, 2026 after a medical emergency at Delaney Hall Detention Facility in Newark, New Jersey -- the 23rd person to die in ICE custody in 2026 and the second death at Delaney Hall since GEO Group reopened the facility under a 15-year, ~$1 billion ICE contract in 2025. Family members and multiple outlets report allegations of medical neglect (a chronic illness allegedly denied treatment); official cause of death is pending. GEO Group owns and directly operates the facility.

top_entities.name: Afghanistan
top_entities.news_summary: Human Rights Watch published "Afghanistan: Taliban Assault on Rights Deepens 5 Years On" on August 3, 2026, marking five years of Taliban rule. Afghanistan remains the only country where girls are barred from secondary education; 21.9 million people require humanitarian assistance in 2026; severe food insecurity now affects 4.7 million people (50% more than the same point last year) including 3.7 million acutely malnourished children; and Pakistan, Iran and Turkey have deported or forcibly returned nearly 5 million Afghans, compounding the crisis. Journalists, activists and perceived critics continue to face arbitrary arrest, detention and torture.

top_entities.name: Georgia
top_entities.news_summary: Pro-European opposition demonstrators held the 612th consecutive day of protests against the Georgian Dream government on August 1, 2026 in Tbilisi's Avlabari Square under the slogan "For a Safe and Strong Georgia," with participants observing a minute's silence for a teenager recently killed in central Tbilisi. The protest movement, ongoing since the October 2024 political crisis, continues amid the government's pursuit of a constitutional supermajority to entrench single-party rule.

top_entities.name: Tbilisi
top_entities.news_summary: The 612th consecutive day of pro-European opposition protests against the Georgian Dream government was held in Tbilisi's Avlabari Square on August 1, 2026, with participants observing a minute's silence for a teenager recently killed in the city. City policing of the sustained protest movement (curfews, detentions over the 21-month campaign) remains an ongoing municipal-level compassion concern distinct from, but linked to, the national government's conduct.

sector_alerts.title: EU AI Act enforcement powers over general-purpose AI models activated
sector_alerts.summary: On August 2, 2026, the European Commission's AI Office became formally entitled to exercise investigation and enforcement powers over providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models and prohibited-practice rules under the EU AI Act, with fines of up to EUR15M or 3% of global turnover for non-compliance. Substantive GPAI obligations had applied since August 2, 2025; this date activates the Office's power to request documentation, evaluate models and mandate corrective measures. Not elevated to an entity-level flag this cycle -- a regulatory-enforcement-window opening is a sector-wide compliance event, not evidence of any specific lab's conduct.

sector_alerts.title: ICE detention deaths continue at record pace; second Delaney Hall death this cycle
sector_alerts.summary: Edwin Lopez-Cornejo's August 1, 2026 death at GEO Group's Delaney Hall facility (Newark, NJ) is the 23rd ICE-custody death of 2026 and the second at Delaney Hall since the facility reopened under a GEO Group contract in 2025 (entity-level flag applied to GEO Group this cycle -- see top_entities). More than 300 detainees at the same facility have separately engaged in hunger/labor strikes over food, medical care and overcrowding conditions in preceding months. Broader context retained here; not double-counted as a separate flag.

sector_alerts.title: State-level expansion of local police 287(g) cooperation with ICE (Missouri, Kansas)
sector_alerts.summary: As of August 3, 2026, 95 Missouri agencies (all signed during the current federal administration) and 36 Kansas agencies now hold Section 287(g) task-force agreements with ICE; Kansas separately enacted a law (over the governor's veto) allowing sheriffs to sign such agreements without county-commission approval. Entity-level flag applied to Missouri this cycle (see top_entities); Kansas retained as sector-level context pending a dedicated dated primary source for a Kansas-specific new development this window.

sector_alerts.title: Compounding climate disasters continue (Europe wildfires, South Asia flooding)
sector_alerts.summary: Wildfires across France and Spain remain the most destructive on record for both countries (679,000+ acres burned, at least three deaths including two firefighters), continuing from the prior cycle. Continued flooding and glacial-lake flood risk in Pakistan, and flash flooding in Liberia, add to a summer of compounding climate disasters per UN OCHA reporting. Retained as continuing sector-level context; no new single-country dated event within window met the threshold for an entity-level flag this cycle.

sector_alerts.title: Healthcare-sector data breaches and ransomware continue climbing
sector_alerts.scope: fortune-500 healthcare/insurance and cross-sector IT vendors
sector_alerts.summary: CareCloud's breach affecting 345,000+ patients continues to generate notifications; multiple new August disclosures (OROVA, INC_RANSOM, Chaos, TheGentlemen-affiliated incidents) were reported industry-wide. A related but distinct incident, the Wesco International/ExfilSquad breach (~2.6M records, occurred July 26, 2026), is elevated to an entity-level flag this cycle (see top_entities) because it names a benchmarked entity directly.

sector_alerts.title: Press freedom crackdowns continue in multiple countries
sector_alerts.summary: The August 1, 2026 enforced disappearance of journalists Razi Tahir and Muhammad Saif in Islamabad (entity-level flag applied to Pakistan this cycle) sits alongside continuing press-freedom deterioration documented by CPJ in the Pakistan-administered-Kashmir reporting environment (internet shutdowns, prior detentions). Retained as sector context for the broader pattern beyond the single dated incident already flagged.
